items.app_analytics: An analytics workspace: a dashboard's filters, headline numbers, a grid of charts and a table under them, walked through by a pointer that changes a filter so every number answers, drills into one bar so the table narrows to it, and exports the view.
items.app_calendar: A calendar at work in week view: days across, hours down, events placed by their times, the guests' free and busy times in a booking form, walked through by a pointer that creates an event, drags one to reschedule it, opens one and invites a colleague.
items.app_chat_workspace: A team chat workspace: channels and direct messages, a channel's conversation with mentions, reactions, file cards and threads, and a composer, walked through by a pointer that opens a channel, posts, reacts and opens a thread.
items.app_cloud_console: A cloud provider's console: services in a sidebar, the project and region, a list of resources with their status, and one resource's detail with its settings, metrics, access roles and logs, walked through by a pointer that creates a resource, scales it, attaches a role and reads its logs.
items.app_docs_editor: A shared document editor: a page of headings, paragraphs and lists, suggested edits shown inline, comments in the margin, and a version history, walked through by a pointer that types, comments on a phrase, accepts a suggestion and restores an earlier version.
items.app_email: An email client at work: folders, a thread list with unread and flagged mail, the open message in a reading pane, and a compose window, walked through by a pointer that opens, replies, flags, moves and searches.
items.app_hris: An HR system an employee and a manager use: the employee's profile with leave balances, a time off request form with past requests, the team's org chart and a manager's approvals queue, walked through by a pointer that requests leave, approves or declines a request and views the team.
items.app_ide_workspace: A developer's workspace: a file tree, editor tabs, code with syntax colour and line numbers, a terminal and a problems list, a source control panel and a debug toolbar, walked through by a pointer that opens a file, runs a command, steps through code in the debugger and commits a change.
items.app_lms_course: An online course on a learning platform: the outline of modules and lessons with what is done, a lesson player, a quiz with feedback, the learner's progress and a certificate, walked through by a pointer that starts a lesson, answers, submits and completes the course.
items.app_project_board: A project tracker a team works in: a board of columns with work-in-progress limits and issue cards, a backlog list, and an issue's detail with its assignee and sub-tasks, walked through by a pointer that creates an issue, drags a card to another column, assigns it and closes it.
items.dev_ci_pipeline: A CI/CD pipeline: stages as cards joined by arrows, each with its jobs, a status icon per job and stage (passed, failed, running, pending, skipped, blocked) and durations; on cue the stages run in order, jobs spin and resolve, and a failed stage stops the flow so the stages after it are skipped.
items.dev_code_editor: A code editor pane: a tab with the file name and its language, line numbers in a gutter, code in syntax colour, an overview stripe and an optional status line; lines type in on cue, a range can be brought into focus, a span marked with a squiggle and a line replaced.
items.dev_db_table: A database table: an optional SQL query bar, column headers with their types, rows of cells with numbers right aligned, the rows past the limit summed up in one line and a row count; on cue the query types and its rows arrive, a filter collapses the rows that do not match, a cell is marked and a column of personal data is masked.
items.dev_diff_view: A code diff: the file's changed hunks with old and new line numbers, removed lines on a faint failure band with a minus, added lines on a faint success band with a plus and context lines plain, unified or side by side; removals then additions reveal on cue and a review comment can open on a row.
items.dev_git_graph: A branch and commit graph: one lane per branch with its name at the left, commits as dots in the order they were made, lines from each commit to its parents (curves where branches fork and merge), tags as small flags and a ring for where HEAD points; commits pop in on cue, a merge draws itself and HEAD travels.
items.dev_http_exchange: An HTTP exchange: a request card with its method, URL, headers and body, and a response card with its status code and reason, headers and body, joined by an arrow with an optional latency; secret header values are masked until revealed, and on cue the request travels and the response arrives.
items.dev_terminal: A terminal session: a window with a title bar, commands typed after a prompt on cue and their output printed under them, errors and successes in their own tones, a block cursor, and lines that scroll when the window is full.

items.power_path: an isometric 2N power chain: two separate paths, A and B, each from its own utility feed through a transformer and switchgear with a transfer switch (its own standby generator wired to that switch), a UPS (the library's ups_cabinet) and an output breaker to its own rack power strip (rack_pdu), ending at one dual-supply server whose two power supplies take one cord from each path; the generators (generator_set) stand outside the lanes
items.rack_pdu: a vertical zero-U rack power strip: a tall housing in its feed's colour, a column of equipment outlets in groups with a light by each, breakers, a small load meter, a feed tag and an input cord with an industrial plug; optionally the A and B pair side by side
items.security_key: a hardware security key: a small rounded fob with a metal connector, a key ring hole and a touch pad that glows
items.server_rack: a server cabinet (v2): a frame holding a column of servers, each with vents and a status light, a top-of-rack switch, a perforated front door, blanking panels for empty units, two vertical power strips A and B and cable bundles at the open rear; air runs front to back
items.shield: a solid heraldic shield with a raised rim and an embossed mark (tick, cross or none)
items.shredder: an office shredder: a bin on casters with a window, a cutting head with a feed slot and a status light; a document feeds into the slot and the shreds fill the bin
items.tablet: a tablet in a slim case standing on its long edge (opts.portrait stands it upright): glass face with a live screen, a case lip round the glass, a camera in the case's corner cut-out
items.tor_switch: a generic 1U top-of-rack network switch: two rows of port cages with link lights and a block of larger uplink cages on the port face; two power supplies and a row of fan modules on the other face; rack ears
items.transformer_stack: a decoder-only transformer as a tower of identical blocks (each an attention slab and a feed-forward slab) on an embedding base, with a residual rail up its side; token tiles rise block by block, one block opens to show its causal attention pattern, and a row of probability bars grows on top with the highest lit
items.ups_cabinet: a generic UPS row cabinet: a power bay with a display and a power-flow mimic, and a battery bay whose door opens on shelves of battery blocks; an input cable and an output cable on top

capabilities.api: storyboard kind "three" with three.preset (params only, nothing to write); py -m loom device <id> <beat> <device> swaps a device beat later
capabilities.when: a ready 3D shot whose content is params: device_shot shows a phone, tablet, laptop, monitor or desk with its screen and moments on spoken words, and the device stays swappable after the storyboard

items.device_shot: one device from the model library, its screen and its moments driven by spoken words; the device, screen and mood are params, so the engine can swap them after the storyboard
items.holo_hero: a hologram hero (hologram v2): one library model shown as projected light on a projector pad (Fresnel rims, its real edges, scan bands, a scan plane that builds it, a hot part, depth fog, bloom and a slight fringe), turning on a turntable, its parts exploding on the word; it exports its parts' screen boxes so the hologram HUD's locks and datums point at them
items.model_shot: one library model or set (assets/models3d) on a lit stage, its keys driven by spoken words; the model, its options, its states and the mood are params, so nothing is written and everything stays swappable
